subject: math
intro: I'm Ms. Chen, 8th grade math. Let's plan a lesson on linear functions that focuses on what slope and y-intercept mean.

beats.narration: I name the concepts in plain language before the formal vocabulary.
This standard asks students to construct a function and interpret rate of change and initial value.
Three representations and interpretation, which is the heart of 8.F.B.4.
beats.text: Students will be able to write a linear function from a context, a table, or a graph and interpret the slope and y-intercept in context.

beats.narration: Students interpret before calculating, which frames the whole lesson.
beats.text: Show a graph of a phone battery draining. "What was the charge at the start? How fast is it dropping?" Students discuss with a partner.

beats.narration: The translation sentence is something I'll ask for all year.
beats.text: Model finding the rate of change from two points and the initial value from the graph. Write y = −8x + 100 and translate: "starts at 100%, loses 8% per hour."

beats.narration: Every group reaches the same function from a different starting point, which makes the connections visible.
beats.text: Taxi fare task: groups get one representation (a story, table, or graph) of a fare and must build the other two plus the equation, then present.

beats.narration: The interpretation question is the real check.
beats.text: A plant is 4 cm tall and grows 1.5 cm per week. Write the function. What do 4 and 1.5 mean?

outro: Interpret, model, connect representations, check. Now it's yours.
